Submarine Manufacturing

partners/)

![](https://www.scouting.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/image-4@3x.png)

## Submarine Manufacturing

## Featured Submarine Manufacturing Merit Badges:

## [Electricity](https://www.scouting.org/merit-badges/electricity/)

## [Engineering](https://www.scouting.org/merit-badges/engineering/)

## [Robotics](https://www.scouting.org/merit-badges/robotics/)

## [Welding](https://www.scouting.org/merit-badges/welding/)

Building submarines is more than just another job — it’s an opportunity to
create powerful underwater vessels that push the boundaries of technology and
exploration. Blending craftsmanship, engineering, and innovation, this field
offers you a chance to be part of something bigger than yourself.



The path to a future in submarine manufacturing can begin today, right where
you are. Working towards merit badges in Electricity, Engineering, Welding, or
Robotics gives you the foundational skills needed to dive deeper into this
exciting industry.  
  
Each badge earned brings you closer to understanding the technologies and
techniques that help build these incredible giants.



[Electricity](/merit-badges/electricity/): Electricity is a vital component in
powering submarines and ensuring their systems operate smoothly beneath the
ocean’s surface. The Electricity Merit Badge offers Scouts the chance to learn
essential electrical skills, like reading an electric meter, that are
foundational to understanding how power systems work on complex machines like
submarines.



[Engineering](/merit-badges/engineering/): Engineers are the architects of the
incredible technology that brings submarines to life, from structural design
to advanced propulsion systems. Through the Engineering Merit Badge, Scouts
can explore how engineers in fields such as mechanical, electrical, and marine
engineering contribute to the creation of submarines, transforming ideas into
vessels capable of exploring the depths of our oceans.



[Welding](/merit-badges/welding/): Welding is essential in submarine
manufacturing, where precision and durability are critical to assembling a
vessel that must withstand immense underwater pressure. The Welding Merit
Badge introduces Scouts to the skills needed for this important trade, showing
how mastering welding can open doors to exciting careers in building
submarines and other high-stakes applications.  
  
[Robotics](/merit-badges/robotics/): Robotics technology is integral to modern
submarines, from automated systems that enhance navigation to remotely
operated vehicles that assist in underwater exploration. The Robotics Merit
Badge allows Scouts to learn about and build their own robots, providing a
glimpse into how robotics are used to perform complex tasks that help
submarines operate effectively in challenging environments.

## Bray Barnes

Director, Global Security Innovative  
Strategies

Bray Barnes is a recipient of the Distinguished Eagle Scout Award, Silver  
Beaver, Silver Antelope, Silver Buffalo, and Learning for Life Distinguished  
Service Award. He received the Messengers of Peace Hero award from  
the royal family of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and he’s a life member of  
the 101st Airborne Association and Vietnam Veterans Association. Barnes  
serves as a senior fellow for the Global Federation of Competitiveness  
Councils, a nonpartisan network of corporate CEOs, university presidents, and  
national laboratory directors. He has also served as a senior executive for
the  
U.S. Department of Homeland Security, leading the first-responder program  
and has two U.S. presidential appointments

Alexander.jpg)![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns=%22http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%22%20viewBox=%220%200%20451%20436%22%3E%3C/svg%3E)

## David Alexander

Managing Member Calje

David Alexander is a Baden-Powell Fellow, Summit Bechtel Reserve
philanthropist, and recipient of the Silver Buffalo and Distinguished Eagle
Scout Award. He is the founder of Caljet, one of the largest independent motor
fuels terminals in the U.S. He has served the Arizona Petroleum Marketers
Association, Teen Lifeline, and American Heart Association. A triathlete who
has completed hundreds of races, Alexander has also mentored the women’s
triathlon team at Arizona State University.

![](https://www.scouting.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/Glenn-
Adams.jpg)![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns=%22http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%22%20viewBox=%220%200%20301%20290%22%3E%3C/svg%3E)

## Glenn Adams

President, CEO & Managing Director  
Stonetex Oil Corp.

Glenn Adams is a recipient of the Silver Beaver, Silver Antelope, Silver
Buffalo, and Distinguished Eagle Scout Award. He is the former president of
the National Eagle Scout Association and established the Glenn A. and Melinda
W. Adams National Eagle Scout Service Project of the Year Award. He has more
than 40 years of experience in the oil, gas, and energy fields, including
serving as a president, owner, and CEO. Adams has also received multiple
service awards from the Texas Alliance of Energy Producers.
